interface.title: Dungeon With Amnesia · Memory Lab (Amnesia Lab Streamlit dashboard)
interface.field: Reinforcement learning / cognitive AI. Memory in recurrent policies under partial observability (POMDPs)
interface.stage_of_work: Exploring and analysing trained (or untrained-preview) PPO agents; causal intervention experiments; reviewing recorded results
interface.what_it_is_for: Run feed-forward, history and recurrent (GRU/LSTM) PPO agents through seeded partially observable dungeons, watch their observations, discovered maps and hidden states, then fork an episode and change the treatment branch's retained memory to test whether memory causes escape success, alongside recorded comparison, ablation and generalisation results.

data.note: Dungeons are generated from a seed (200000 by default). No checkpoints are bundled, so every architecture ran as an 'Untrained policy preview' with a warning banner, and a typed checkpoint path that does not exist was ignored. All live runs and all memory interventions in this record therefore used untrained-preview policies. The Experiment results tab shows recorded CSVs and plots committed in the repo (showcase and comparison families); the memory reset and noise ablation plots are the fixed showcase GRU ablation and do not change with the family. One file was downloaded: paired_trace.json (189 KB), holding control and treatment metrics, config, and a per-step timeline with observation, hidden vector and action probabilities.

tree.general: Find out whether an agent's retained internal state causally drives its success on a task where a cue is shown only once and must be remembered after it leaves view
tree.specific: Test whether GRU/LSTM hidden state is what lets the PPO agent carry the one-time seal cue (e.g. RAVEN / MOON), which is no longer in its observation later, through to escaping the amnesia dungeon, compared with MLP and history policies
